title: Concurrent Tenant Quota and Fairness Playbook for Private Deployments
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes Redwood's recommended policies, configuration patterns, and operational procedures for enforcing concurrent-tenant quotas and fairness in private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It focuses on multi-customer sharing of GPU pools, predictable latency for tenant SLAs, cost transparency, and safe escalation paths for quota-related incidents. The guidance applies to both hosted control-plane-managed private deployments and fully air-gapped on-prem bundles.

Scope and intent:
- Prevent noisy-neighbor effects in shared inference pools while preserving utilization.
- Provide a clear mapping from business-level entitlements (committed vCPU/GPU units, burst windows, priority tiers) to runtime enforcement knobs.
- Offer deterministic operational procedures for emergency throttling, quota adjustments, and fairness audits during incidents and capacity changes.

When to use this playbook:
1) Customer requests: shared-GPU private deployment where multiple internal teams or customer tenants run inference workloads on the same cluster.
2) Observed tail latency or token throughput variance correlated with tenant workload spikes.
3) Pre-launch capacity validation for new tenant onboarding to identify fairness violations.

Definitions:
- Tenant: A logical customer (could be an internal business unit or external customer) with an isolated API key and billing account.
- Entitlement: Contractual or configured resource allocation (e.g., 2 reserved GPUs, 10 max concurrent generation requests).
- Soft quota: Dynamic throttling thresholds that can be exceeded briefly by burst policy.
- Hard quota: Enforced reject/fail path when exceeded.
- Fairshare window: Time window used to calculate proportional resource distribution (default: 5 minutes).

Design principles:
- Favor proportional fairshare over strict absolute caps to maximize utilization while bounding worst-case interference.
- Expose transparent metrics and quota usage per tenant to customers where allowed by confidentiality agreements.
- Provide graceful degradation: fall back to lower-cost model variant or lower max tokens before rejecting.
- Separate priority (SLA) from entitlement; priority affects preemption/reservation, entitlement is billing/accounting.

Configuration reference (example YAML snippet for quota controller):

quotaController:
  fairshare_window_seconds: 300  # 5 minutes
  per_tenant:
    default:
      max_concurrent_requests: 8
      max_total_tokens_per_minute: 20000
      soft_burst_multiplier: 2
      hard_reject: true
    enterprise-tier:
      max_concurrent_requests: 32
      max_total_tokens_per_minute: 200000
      soft_burst_multiplier: 3
      hard_reject: false
  eviction_policy:
    - name: low_priority_preempt
      priority_threshold: 20
      actions:
        - reduce_batch_size: 0.5
        - lower_model_variant: amd/quantized-8bit

Notes on fields:
- max_concurrent_requests: concurrency at the inference request level (requests that are currently holding KV-cache slots).
- soft_burst_multiplier: allows short bursts; quota controller will apply backpressure via 429 + Retry-After when sustained.

Monitoring & observability:
Essential metrics (Prometheus names given):
- tenant_quota_utilization{tenant_id} = gauge of usage / entitlement
- tenant_concurrency_active{tenant_id} = number of in-flight requests
- tenant_token_rate{tenant_id} = tokens/sec rolling mean
- quota_controller_rejections_total{tenant_id,reason}
- fairshare_score{tenant_id} = internal calculated fairness factor

Example PromQL alerts:
- High sustained concurrency for tenant:
  sum by (tenant_id) (tenant_concurrency_active) > 0 and avg_over_time(tenant_concurrency_active[10m]) > 0.9 * on(tenant_id) group_left() tenant_entitlement_concurrency
- Quota rejections spike (indicative of misconfigured entitlements):
  increase(quota_controller_rejections_total[5m]) > 10

Operational procedures (step-by-step):
1) Detection: automated alert triggers on quota rejections spike or sustained tail-latency across tenants.
2) Triage: on-call reviews Grafana dashboard: per-tenant concurrency, fairshare_score, model_variant distribution, node GPU load.
3) Fast mitigation (first 15 minutes):
   a) Enable global soft-throttling (reduce default soft_burst_multiplier to 1).
   b) If a single tenant is responsible, apply per-tenant temporary hard cap (e.g., set max_concurrent_requests=2) with a TTL of 30 minutes. Record change in incident channel.
   c) If cluster-wide contention, trigger autoscale (if allowed) or move low-priority pods to reserve pool.
4) Customer communication: Send templated status update to affected tenants with observed metrics, mitigation steps, and ETA for resolution.
5) Root cause & remediation (post-30 minutes):
   a) If a tenant is misbehaving repeatedly, schedule a billing/entitlement review.
   b) Adjust fairshare_window_seconds or reserve capacity for enterprise-tier tenants.
   c) Update runbook with any new thresholds discovered.

Safe rollback and escalation:
- Immediate rollback of quota controller changes: use the controller's versioned configstore. Command example:
  # rollback to previous config version
  rcli quota-config rollback --to-version=v21 --env=prod
- If config rollback fails or controller is unreachable:
  1) Flip global feature-flag to bypass fairshare controller and fall back to absolute per-tenant hard-caps (emergency limit).
  2) If the API gateway shows overload, enable 503-fastfail for non-enterprise tiers for 3 minutes while mitigation runs.

Sample CLI snippets for on-prem appliance (control-plane managed):
- Inspect current per-tenant usage:
  rcli tenant list-usage --format=table --filter="tenant:acme-corp"
- Apply a temporary hard cap:
  rcli quota set --tenant acme-corp --max-concurrent-requests 4 --ttl 30m --reason "Emergency mitigation"

Fairness audit and monthly reconciliation:
- Run monthly audit job to detect persistent unfairness (script runs nightly and emits a report):
  1) Compute 95th-percentile fairshare_score per tenant for the month.
  2) Flag tenants with score < 0.6 and > 3 incidents for manual review.
  3) Generate CSV for billing and product ops to reconcile entitlements vs usage.

Capacity planning knobs (recommendations):
- Reserve 10% of physical GPU capacity as "headroom" for eviction/burst handling.
- For mixed workloads (short chat vs long-completion), isolate long-token workloads into a dedicated node-pool labeled "long-running" and enforce stricter per-tenant token-rate caps.
- Use multi-queue scheduling: separate small-batch low-latency queue vs large-batch high-throughput queue, and map tenants based on SLAs.

Security, privacy, and compliance considerations:
- Do not expose per-tenant payloads in shared dashboards; only surface aggregated quota and latency metrics unless customer consent exists.
- Store quota change audit logs in the control plane KMS-encrypted audit store (retention 13 months for enterprise customers).

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments Day-2-ops (owner: Asha Patel)
- SRE escalation: eng-sre on-call (pager rotation)
- Product/billing reviews: customer-success and finance-legal for entitlement disputes

Post-incident analysis checklist:
- Time-series graphs: fairshare_score, per-tenant concurrency, node_gpu_utilization for the incident window.
- Configuration diffs: compare quota controller versions and list any manual per-tenant overrides.
- Customer impact: enumerated tenants affected, duration, tokens lost or rejected.
- Action items: carry-forward changes, timeline for reserved capacity purchase, API changes if necessary.

Appendix A — Example fairshare calculation (simplified):
- For N tenants, each tenant i has entitlement E_i. Compute weight w_i = E_i / sum(E). Over fairshare_window_seconds, allocate capacity proportionally by w_i. If tenant exceeds 2x w_i in any sub-window, apply soft throttle.

Appendix B — Emergency contact templates:
- Slack: "@channel Incident: quota rejections spike. Mitigation: per-tenant caps applied to tenant=acme-corp. Owner: Asha Patel. ETA 30m. See dashboard: <grafana-link>"
- Email: short templated incident summary to customer-facing leads for affected tenants.

Appendix C — Related configuration files and locations:
- /etc/redwood/quota-controller/config.yaml (cluster-local copy)
- s3://redwood-controlplane/backups/quota-configs/ (retention 90 days)

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12: Initial draft and trial runbook (Asha Patel).
- 2025-11-03: Added PromQL alert examples and soft_burst semantics (Liam Chen).
- 2026-02-08: Hardened rollback steps and added per-tenant TTL policy for overrides (Sofia Martinez).

End of document.
